title: Operator Memory
idiom: Ravilious-like dry-brush watercolour, a tide line of keepsakes below a stone house
hero_prompt: Dry-brush watercolour in the manner of Eric Ravilious, pale chalky washes with a dry scratchy brush, hand-made on paper, flat and graphic with visible brush and paper texture, not a photograph, not a 3D render, no depth-of-field, wide panoramic composition: a wide empty beach at low tide with a thin foamy wave edge sliding up the wet sand; just before the wave, laid in a row on the sand, three small things, a brass key, a feather and a scallop shell, about to be washed away; higher up the beach on a grassy dune stands a small stone cottage with one warm lit window, and a scallop shell already rests safe on its doorstep, while a woman in a headscarf, seen small and from behind, walks up the sand toward it carrying a basket. Pale grey-blue, sand and faded green; lots of open sky.
icon_prompt: Linocut emblem, a flat single-colour black silhouette on a pale grey-blue ground, no shading or gradients: a small house with a door standing on a mound, and one large curling wave reaching toward it from the left. Bold, high-contrast, no fine linework, reads clearly at 24 pixels.
